findings.rationale: CA's uploaded updates are about 10-12x the median norm in every round (round 1 norm_ratio 16.82), while its update direction is essentially uncorrelated with the consensus (mean cos 0.058, swinging between about -0.8 and +0.5 across rounds). That pattern matches large random noise added to uploads rather than honest training. Its local performance is normal (AUC 0.8312, CITL 0.005), so the noise is not coming from bad labels or drift, and the global accuracy is not visibly affected.

IA's update norms are about 9x the median across the federation (median norm_ratio 9.408, min 6.587, size-adjusted z +11.2 to +12.5), and the mean cosine to the consensus update is near zero (0.1032). This is the random-noise signature of explanation instability rather than a sign-flip, because a scaled honest update would keep a cosine near the federation norm of about 0.5. Local AUC (0.8453) and CITL (0.0089) are normal.

SC's update norms are about 10x the median (median norm_ratio 10.62, min 7.32, size-adjusted z +11.9 to +13.4), with a mean cosine to the consensus of only 0.1501 and some strongly negative rounds (min -0.3186). The pattern is consistent with large random noise in uploads. Local performance is not degraded (AUC 0.7994, CITL -0.019, within the federation spread).

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex and AgeGroup), then confirmed suspicions with narrower queries. The budget is fully spent (20.0). Three clients (CA, IA, SC) show update norms about 9-12x the federation median with near-zero cosine to the consensus, and their local performance is normal. This points to explanation_instability (large random noise in uploads), not label noise or drift, so I report them with onset round 1; the onset for IA and SC comes from whole-run summaries rather than per-round data, so it is less certain. Several small clients (GU, VI, CT, DE, and some feature-tail outliers) showed weak or inconsistent flags. Their signals did not reproduce across calls or sat near the noise floor, so I did not report them as faulty. GU has one round with a norm_ratio of 0 and cos of 1 in the narrow query, which could indicate free-riding, but the 20-round summary shows a minimum norm_ratio of 0.32 and the signal is too noisy to support a finding.
